answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a bond that is locked until it completes a randomly assigned task, then slash the bond if independent reviewers find fabricated work. A public beacon can commit to the task seed before identities register, preventing an attacker from choosing easy tasks afterward. Whether the bond is called jade or opal, each extra sybil ties up real capital and risks forfeiture, so multiplying identities becomes costly rather than free.
